I have also a workaround:
1. Create a persistence.xml (which seems to be picked up by quarkus):

`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<persistence version="2.1" xmlns="http://xmlns.jcp.org/xml/ns/persistence" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://xmlns.jcp.org/xml/ns/persistence http://xmlns.jcp.org/xml/ns/persistence/persistence_2_1.xsd">
  <persistence-unit name="test" transaction-type="JTA">
    <provider>org.hibernate.jpa.HibernatePersistenceProvider</provider>
    <exclude-unlisted-classes>true</exclude-unlisted-classes>
    <shared-cache-mode>NONE</shared-cache-mode>
    <properties>
      <property name="hibernate.show_sql" value="true"/>
      <property name="hibernate.dialect" value="org.hibernate.dialect.PostgreSQL10Dialect"/>
      <property name="javax.persistence.validation.mode" value="NONE"/>
      <property name="javax.persistence.schema-generation.create-source" value="script-then-metadata"/>
      <property name="javax.persistence.schema-generation.database.action" value="create"/>
      <property name="javax.persistence.schema-generation.create-script-source" value="create.sql"/>
    </properties>
  </persistence-unit>
</persistence>`

and inside the create.sql you create the schema:
create schema if not exists myschema;

Yes schema creation is seen as an administrative task very much like the database creation.

Using a `persistence.xml` is not really recommended.

I suppose we would have to expose `javax.persistence.schema-generation.create-script-source` in the config.

N.B. there's the possibility that the reported issue is caused by a different problem, like our lack of full db metadata. I'd need to investigate better.

Take a look at https://docs.jboss.org/hibernate/orm/5.2/userguide/html_single/Hibernate_User_Guide.html#schema-generation

> javax.persistence.create-database-schemas (e.g. true or false (default value))
The JPA variant of hibernate.hbm2dll.create_namespaces. Specifies whether the persistence provider is to create the database schema(s) in addition to creating database objects (tables, sequences, constraints, etc). The value of this boolean property should be set to true if the persistence provider is to create schemas in the database or to generate DDL that contains "CREATE SCHEMA" commands. If this property is not supplied (or is explicitly false), the provider should not attempt to create database schemas.

To summarize a couple of things about this functionality:

1. Schema creation only happens if you set `javax.persistence.create-database-schemas=true`.
2. According to the JPA spec, apparently, it only happens if you explicitly set the schema of all your entities using `@Table(name="foo", schema="bar")`, which is pretty sucky.
3. But Hibernate has a better way which is to set `hibernate.default_schema`. Fortunately Quarkus exposes this already as `quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.default-schema`.
4. Schema creation does work on Postgres, but I question how many databases it really works on. It doesn't work on MySQL or DB2.
5. You can automatically create the catalog on (only) MySQL, however. (Exposed in Quarkus as `quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.default-catalog`.)

So if we expose `quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.generation.create-namespaces`, we are good, I think.

By the way, I don't love the way the schema export settings are grouped under "database". We're not generating a database, we're inferring and exporting a schema _to_ the database.
